title: Transport abstraction interface (Go)
description: Create comp/pipelinesink/impl/transport.go defining the Transport interface (Send([]byte) error, Close() error) and unixTransport implementing it. unixTransport must maintain a persistent connection to the Unix socket with exponential backoff reconnect (100ms initial, 2x multiplier, 30s cap). If Send is called while disconnected it must return an error immediately (no blocking). Include a Dial method. The reconnect loop must be goroutine-leak-free (cancelable via context).
success_criteria: `go build ./comp/pipelinesink/impl/` exits 0
Unit test: start a local Unix socket server, create unixTransport, call Send — assert message received
Unit test: start unixTransport with no server running — Send returns a non-nil error within 10ms
Unit test: server starts 200ms after transport — transport reconnects automatically and Send succeeds
Goroutine leak test: goleak.VerifyNone after Close() — no goroutines left behind
Benchmark: `go test -bench=BenchmarkTransportSend -benchtime=5s ./comp/pipelinesink/impl/` reports ≥ 500000 ns/op-level throughput (i.e., ≥ 500k sends/s on loopback)

title: Signal batcher with ring buffers (Go)
description: Create comp/pipelinesink/impl/batcher.go. Implement a Batcher struct that holds per-type ring buffers (metrics and logs) with configurable capacity (default 1000). AddMetric/AddLog methods are called from hook callbacks and must return immediately. A background flush goroutine drains buffers every flushInterval, encodes batches via encoder.go, and calls Transport.Send(). When a ring buffer is full the oldest item is overwritten (not newest dropped) and a drop counter increments. The goroutine must be stoppable via Stop() with a clean shutdown (no goroutine leaks).
success_criteria: `go build ./comp/pipelinesink/impl/` exits 0
Unit test: Add 5 metrics, wait 150ms — assert Transport.Send called with a MetricBatch containing 5 samples
Unit test: Add capacity+10 metrics before flush — assert drop counter == 10, sent count == capacity
Unit test: Stop() with no goroutine leaks (goleak.VerifyNone)
Unit test: flush when transport returns error — drop counter increments, no panic
Benchmark: `go test -bench=BenchmarkBatcherAdd -benchtime=5s ./comp/pipelinesink/impl/` reports ≥ 1000000 AddMetric calls/s (i.e., AddMetric ns/op ≤ 1000)

title: sink.go constructor and hook subscriptions
description: Create comp/pipelinesink/impl/sink.go with NewComponent(req Requires) (Provides, error). When pipelinesink.enabled=false, return a no-op implementation that satisfies the Component interface but does nothing. When enabled, subscribe to all hooks via fxutil.GetAndFilterGroup, copy payloads into the batcher, start the flush goroutine, and register lifecycle start/stop hooks. Follow the exact pattern from comp/anomalydetection/recorder/impl/recorder.go.
success_criteria: `go build ./comp/pipelinesink/impl/` exits 0
Unit test: NewComponent with enabled=false returns no-op component; Stats() returns zero Stats
Unit test: NewComponent with enabled=true and a mock hook — publish a metric — assert batcher receives it
Unit test: lifecycle Stop() drains the batcher and closes transport
Unit test: two hook instances subscribed — both receive payloads independently
Benchmark: `go test -bench=BenchmarkSinkObserveMetric ./comp/pipelinesink/impl/` — hook callback overhead ≤ 500ns/op (copy + enqueue only)
